subject: Fix bug in the mctp-demux-daemon client management logic

comments.message:
Patch Set 1:

User not approved, see admin, no CI

Hi Ken, thanks for the patch. CI hasn't triggered in this case because you're not recognised as having signed a CLA for contributions to OpenBMC. There's more info on the process here:

https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#starting-out

Are you happy to do so? Generally we encourage a corporate CLA if that suits your circumstances. If not an individual CLA is also fine.

Hi Andrew, thanks for reviewing the patch and enlightening me about the contribution process.
Sure, I'm happy to sign a CLA. I will ask my employer (Napatech) if they are okay with executing a corporate one. I will get back to you.

Hi @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au, my employer asks about the apparent dual licenses scheme used by OpenBMC. It says "Apache-2.0" or "GPLv2+" license.
Which one is it, or do both apply in the sense that you are free to adhere to the one you prefer? If you are the right person to answer this question? Thanks.

The formal definition for disjunctive `OR` in a composite SPDX license expression is here:

https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/annexes/spdx-license-expressions/#disjunctive-or-operator

Some practical examples are here:

https://spdx.dev/learn/handling-license-info/#how

The crux of the expression found at e.g. https://gerrit.openbmc.org/plugins/gitiles/openbmc/libmctp/+/aa174c4f9f3f75d7901bdbf8e84797b9a39b9364/utils/mctp-demux-daemon.c#1 is that you may consider the software licensed under the most appropriate license for your circumstances out of the options specified.

Cheers for the clarification. Much appreciated.
Just FYI, the process of getting a Corporate CLA signed is stalled a bit because one guy is out traveling this week and next week. But I'll keep you posted hopefully soon after he's back.

But actually, one question that did arise regarding the Corporate CLA, is whether submitting this CLA is a one-time event, or it has to be done for any consecutive contributions we might have.
My understanding is that it's a one-time thing, and all the individuals we list in "Schedule A" will be able to contribute on a consecutive basis, without having to submit a new CLA each time. Is this correctly understood? You know?
Sorry to bug you with all these question.

> But actually, one question that did arise regarding the Corporate CLA, is whether submitting this CLA is a one-time event, or it has to be done for any consecutive contributions we might have.

It must be adjusted whenever you change the listed CLA managers or contributors. Otherwise, it is effectively a one-time event.

> My understanding is that it's a one-time thing, and all the individuals we list in "Schedule A" will be able to contribute on a consecutive basis, without having to submit a new CLA each time. Is this correctly understood?

Yes, that's correct.

> Sorry to bug you with all these question.

No problems, best if they're clarified 😊

Excellent, thanks a lot!
One final question (I hope) regarding "Schedule B" then. We are a bit uncertain in which circumstances one would fill in this one. Could you perhaps please clarify?
Specifically for our actual case, should we fill in a description of the contribution (i.e. bugfix) we intend to make to libmctp? Or should we state something more general about what we foresee to contribute with going forward? Or simply leave it blank? 😊
Thanks.
I'm not in a position to offer advice there. I recommend you email the query to the project mailing list.

Hi @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au,

We at Napatech (the company I work for) have finally managed to get the Corporate CLA submitted and approved.

I should therefore now be all clear to contribute this patch under my company email address: "kw@napatech.com".

Now, however unfortunately when I created the patch, I used my private email address. So "Owner" and "Signed-off-by" in the commit message has the wrong value.
What's the best way to correct these fields? Can it be done with the "edit" function directly here i Gerrit? Or do I push a change, or entirely new patch, with the corrected signature?

Hi @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au,

I figured it was best to upload a new patch with the correct user and company email address. Please see: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libmctp/+/80369

I will abandon this patch once the other one is approved.
